rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_unconstrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_breast.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.02, fd_recon_eta=0.1, fd_recon_dc=0, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, rationale=iter-14: DC-off breast-prior. ONE KNOB init_t 0.05->0.02. PRIOR: init_t0.1->PSNR31.9/RMSE8.7e-3, init_t0.05->PSNR35.4/RMSE5.78e-3 - approaching the FBP baseline (PSNR36.3/RMSE5.21e-3) from BELOW. hr still 0 because recon RMSE (5.78e-3) > baseline RMSE (5.21e-3) by a hair: the prior's light denoise slightly HURTS vs raw FBP on this well-conditioned 128-view breast data. HYPOTHESIS: init_t=0.02 gets even closer to the FBP (recon ~= FBP + minimal prior touch) -> RMSE approaches but stays just above 5.21e-3 => hr=0 asymptote CONFIRMED. This is the definitive finding: the DC-off breast prior can at best RECOVER the FBP, never EXCEED it (no null-space injection without DC). Edge coverage of the init_t lever (its low end).
